source: Li, Zhang, Fan, Jiao et al. (2025) Understanding the Thinking Process of Reasoning Models: A Perspective from Schoenfeld's Episode Theory
finding: First hand-labelled corpus of reasoning-model traces with Schoenfeld episodes: 7 sentence labels (Read, Analyze, Plan, Implement, Explore, Verify, Monitor) and 3 paragraph labels (General, Explore, Verify). Monitor is the added metacognitive label for short hesitation sentences between episodes.
numbers: 38 DeepSeek-R1 responses to SAT maths problems; 915 paragraphs; 3,087 sentences.
limits: SAT maths only (moderate difficulty); one model's traces; labels are descriptive and were not linked to correctness in this paper.
agent_relevance: Gives a ready 7-label code book we can reuse to tag our own agent logs. Monitor is the label closest to our impasse signal.

source: Li et al. (2025) Schoenfeld episodes paper, Table 2 (prompting conditions)
finding: Giving the annotator LLM a detailed guidebook raised accuracy far more than giving examples. Zero-shot labelling is poor (sentence accuracy 0.48 to 0.60).
numbers: GPT-4.1 sentence acc: base 0.595, examples 0.604, guidebook 0.676, examples+guidebook 0.681 (paragraph acc 0.444, 0.559, 0.740, 0.757). GPT-4o sentence: 0.475, 0.504, 0.577, 0.609. Gemini-2.0: 0.590, 0.628, 0.655, 0.626.
limits: Table 2 numbers (0.681 best) differ from the 0.805 headline in Table 4; Table 4 is on a 30% test subset, the paper does not explain the gap clearly. Gemini was best with guidebook alone.
agent_relevance: A live episode tagger needs a written definition guide, not just examples. Budget for ~0.7 accuracy, so use only coarse, count-based signals from it.

source: Li et al. (2025) Schoenfeld episodes paper, Table 4 (classifier comparison)
finding: Best sentence labeller was GPT-4.1 with examples and guidebook; a fine-tuned BERT came close and is cheap to run. Training-based classifiers on Gemini embeddings were worse.
numbers: Sentence accuracy / Cohen kappa on 30% held-out test: GPT-4.1 0.805 / 0.764; BERT 0.732 / 0.671; RoBERTa 0.730 / 0.670; SVM 0.704 / 0.632; MLP 0.684 / 0.613; KNN 0.587 / 0.490. Training set was 70% of the small corpus.
limits: Test set is under 1,000 sentences from 38 traces; the same problems' traces appear on both sides of the split, so BERT may be optimistic.
agent_relevance: A small BERT tagger (0.73) is a no-LLM-call option for the code-checked detector; cost matters because the schema says the program, not the model, decides transitions.

source: Li et al. (2025) Schoenfeld episodes paper, Figure 1 and confusion matrices
finding: Common transitions in the gold labels: Read to Analyze, Plan to Implement, Explore to Analyze. Even the best labeller confuses Analyze with Verify and Implement with Verify. Monitor sentences are followed by many different labels (no strong next step).
numbers: Gold sentence transition row for Plan: Implement 0.40 (about); Implement row: stays Implement 0.63; Explore row: Analyze 0.25, stays Explore 0.34; Verify row: stays Verify 0.51.
limits: Matrix from 3,087 sentences, one model; self-transition dominates.
agent_relevance: Verify is the hardest label to separate from calculation. A detector should not rely on single Verify tags; use runs and transitions.

source: Li, Fan, Cheng, Feizi, Zhou (2025/2026) Schoenfeld's Anatomy of Mathematical Reasoning by Language Models (ThinkARM)
finding: Scaled the episode analysis: 8 labels (adds Answer), sentence-level only, GPT-5 as annotator, 15 models on 100 Omni-MATH problems. Reasoning traces show a three-phase heartbeat: Read/Analyze/Plan first, Implement peak, then Verify and Monitor surge before Answer.
numbers: 1,500 responses; 410,991 sentences; gold set 9 problems, 7,067 hand-labelled sentences. Annotator accuracy/kappa on gold (reasoning models): GPT-5 86.02/82.54, GPT-4.1 85.75/82.39, Gemini-2.5-Flash 82.45/78.21, Gemini-2.5-Pro 80.53/75.60. Non-reasoning subset: GPT-5 89.34/85.35.
limits: Annotator is an LLM (GPT-5), labelling noise remains; maths only; gold set covers 9 of 100 problems.
agent_relevance: Shows a labelled-episode pipeline is now reliable (kappa about 0.8) with a full guidebook plus previous labels as context. Our log tagger can copy that design.

source: ThinkARM (2025) Table 2 and Section 3.3 episode coverage
finding: Reasoning models differ from instruction models in how effort is split, not only in length. Instruction models spend most tokens on Implement; reasoning models spread over Analyze, Explore, Verify. Distilled models keep the teacher's allocation across sizes. Proprietary reasoning models seen only through final answers look like non-reasoning models.
numbers: R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B example: Analyze 26.93%, Implement 34.39%, Explore 13.23%, Verify 11.43%, Monitor 1.84% of tokens (9,897 tokens avg).
limits: Proprietary models give no thinking tokens, so their rows are not comparable.
agent_relevance: Our scaffold can target the allocation of a reasoning model: more Analyze/Verify, bounded Explore. Hidden-thinking models cannot be tagged from outside.

source: ThinkARM (2025) Section 4.1 and Tables 4 and 13, correctness case study
finding: Lasso logistic regression on episode features predicts correctness. Positive: Explore to Monitor, Explore to Analyze, Monitor to Analyze, Read to Verify, Answer to Verify. Negative: high Explore ratio, Explore to Verify (checking before a hypothesis is consolidated), Implement to Read (re-reading after execution breaks down).
numbers: 500 stratified traces from 5 open reasoning models; 64 transition + 8 ratio + 3 global features. Example coefficients: Read to Verify +0.27, Ratio(Think) +0.22, Ans to Verify +0.22, Ratio(Ver) +0.21; negatives: Count(Total) -0.36, Imp to Read -0.32, Imp to Imp -0.28, Ana to Mon -0.26, Ver to Read -0.25, Ver to Plan -0.25.
quote: sustained exploration without subsequent stabilization is associated with incorrect outcomes
limits: Association only; no held-out accuracy, AUC or intervention reported in text read; 500 traces; top 3 coefficients not extracted; confounded with problem difficulty and total length (Count(Total) is itself a strong negative).
agent_relevance: Directly supplies candidate impasse features: long Explore without Monitor/Analyze after it, Implement then Read, Explore then Verify. Needs our own test before it becomes a guardrail trigger.

source: ThinkARM (2025) Section 4.2 and Tables 5 and 6, efficiency case study
finding: Shortening methods are not neutral. L1 and ThinkPrune cut Verify and Analyze loops (such as Analyze-Verify-Analyze) strongly; Arora and Zanette's method keeps the baseline transition shape and diverges least.
numbers: Tokens per response: base R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B 9,897; L1 2,437; ThinkPrune 4,054; A&Z 5,312. Divergence score top pattern: L1 N-V-N 0.3762, ThinkPrune N-V-N 0.1506, A&Z M-E 0.1039.
limits: Accuracy of the pruned models is not weighed against pattern loss in the text read; 1.5B models only.
agent_relevance: Warns that a token cap in our scaffold removes verification loops first. Cap Explore, protect Verify (guardrail G3/G2 idea).

source: ThinkARM (2025) Section 3.2 and Appendix, easier-problem check (GSM8K)
finding: On easy problems non-reasoning models skip reflective checking nearly entirely; the reasoning-mode Qwen3-32B puts over half its budget in Verify.
numbers: 50 GSM8K problems: Qwen3-32B reasoning mode 55.89% of tokens on Verify; Gemini-2.0-Flash 55.58% on Implement; Explore and Verify about 0 for Gemini-2.0-Flash and Qwen3-32B non-reasoning.
limits: 4 models, 50 problems.
agent_relevance: Verify share grows when execution is cheap; supports a fixed verification budget decided by code, not by the model.

source: Chen, Xu et al. (2024) Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Defines overthinking with outcome efficiency (tokens to first correct answer over total) and process efficiency (share of tokens in distinct strategies). Later solutions rarely add new strategies. Self-training (SimPO with first-correct and diversity-preserving data) cuts tokens about 45% with small accuracy cost.
numbers: QwQ-32B-Preview '2+3': 13 solutions, 7 strategies, 901 tokens, first correct at token 39 (outcome eff 4.3%, process eff 35.8%). MATH500 baseline QwQ: 93.0 acc, 2,407.9 tokens, outcome 52.3%. After FCS+Reflection: 92.8 acc, 1,330.7 tokens (44.7% fewer). AIME24 46.7 to 43.3 acc, 9,480.9 to 5,154.5 tokens. o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens than conventional on easy items.
limits: Only two o1-like models analysed, one post-trained; segmentation by Llama-3.3-70B and clustering by GPT-4o; paper text has an inconsistency (48.6% quoted for MATH500, table says 44.7%).
agent_relevance: Gives a code-computable stuck signal: share of tokens after the first correct answer. Our agent can stop on 'second agreeing answer' rather than letting the model keep verifying.

source: Wang, Liu, Chen et al. (2025) Thoughts Are All Over the Place: On the Underthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Wandering in the other direction: models jump between thoughts before finishing a promising one. Wrong answers contain far more thought switches and tokens. A decoding penalty on switch words ('alternatively') improves accuracy without training.
numbers: Incorrect responses use about 225% more tokens and 418% more thought switches than correct ones. Over 70% of incorrect responses hold at least one correct thought. Underthinking score (share of tokens after first correct thought, wrong answers): AIME24 R1 37.0, QwQ 65.0; MATH500-Hard R1 65.4. TIP (alpha 3, beta 600): AIME24 QwQ 38.3 to 44.1, R1-Distill-32B 61.4 to 64.1, R1 73.8 to 74.8; with 4-sample self-consistency QwQ 43.7 to 51.4. R1 switch tokens 13.8 to 5.7.
quote: frequently switch between different reasoning thoughts without sufficiently exploring promising paths
limits: AIME24 has 30 problems; correctness judge validated on 90 items at about 82%; hyperparameters tuned on one model and dataset; gains are 0.5 to 6 points.
agent_relevance: Counter-weight to overthinking: some failure is early abandonment. Impasse detector needs both too-many-switches and too-long-without-switch, and G1 'doubt only on signal' agrees with limiting switches.

source: Pipis et al. (2025) Wait, Wait, Wait... Why Do Reasoning Models Loop?
finding: Repetition loops are mostly errors in learning, not decoding noise alone. Loops are more common with greedy or low-temperature decoding, in smaller models, and in distilled students even when the teacher rarely loops. Higher temperature lowers loops but does not fix the cause.
numbers: Abstract gave no numeric rates.
limits: Only abstract page opened this session; no numbers captured.
agent_relevance: Loops are an expected failure for small models in our loop; a code-side repeated-text detector with a forced reset is justified, and sampling temperature should not be zero for retries.

source: Cuesta-Ramirez, Beaussant, Mounsif (2025) Large Reasoning Models are not thinking straight (KONVENS 2025)
finding: Even when the correct solution is injected into the chain of thought after each thought, models keep generating and often move off it. Acceptance of the injected answer was rare.
numbers: 3 models (two R1-distilled, LLaMA 70B and Qwen 7B; DeepScaleR-1.5B RL-trained) on AIME2024; positive acceptance observed 'only twice' in a DeepScaleR example; one wrong statement appeared about 3,000 tokens after the injected ground truth. Thoughts split at 'Alternatively' and 'Wait'.
limits: Math only, few models, no aggregate rates, figure captions inconsistent (three vs four models).
agent_relevance: Models do not reliably recognize a correct answer in their own context. Supports G2/G3: a checker in code, not self-judgement, must end the search.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Know When They're Right: Probing Hidden States for Self-Verification
finding: A small probe on the last hidden state of each chunk predicts whether the intermediate answer is correct, even though the model keeps going. Used as an early-exit rule it saves tokens at equal accuracy.
numbers: In-distribution ROC-AUC above 0.7 for all, above 0.9 for R1-Distill-Qwen-32B on AIME. R1-Distill-Llama-8B on MATH: threshold 0.85 gives 88.2% accuracy (equal to no early exit) with about 24% fewer tokens; at matched budget 87.4% vs 82.5% static exit. Cross-dataset: GSM8K probe on MATH AUC 0.80; on AIME 0.69 (ECE 0.25).
limits: Needs hidden states (open models only); labels from Gemini 2.0 Flash; chunking by keywords like 'wait'; AIME test sets 25 to 30 items; one model and dataset for early exit.
agent_relevance: Evidence the correctness signal exists but is unused. For API models we cannot probe; the code-checked answer agreement is our substitute.

source: Yang et al. (2025) Dynamic Early Exit in Reasoning Models (DEER)
finding: Training-free loop: watch for transition words ('Wait', 'Alternatively'), prompt the model for a trial answer at that point, and stop if answer confidence is above 0.95. This is a coded episode-boundary detector inside a generation loop.
numbers: Confidence threshold 0.95 (stable 0.9 to 0.97 on MATH-500); R1-Distill-Qwen-7B overall accuracy 64.2 to 69.2 with 61.5% of tokens kept; Qwen3-14B 82.8 to 83.7 (57.1% kept); QwQ-32B 82.6 to 84.0 (80.9% kept). Latency cut 27.9 to 40.1%.
limits: Weak on hard tasks and code; confidence noisy for small models; the paper's abstract and body give different compression ranges.
agent_relevance: The closest working example of 'act on a signal at an episode boundary, not on a schedule' (G1). Trial answer at each Wait is a code-controlled Verify.

source: Ghosal et al. (2025) Does Thinking More Always Help? Understanding Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning Models
finding: Forcing extra 'Wait' thinking raises accuracy at first, then lowers it as output variance grows. Splitting the same budget over independent short paths and voting does better.
numbers: GSM-8K, R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B: accuracy 82.2% at 385 tokens, 87.3% at 1,100 tokens, 70.3% at 15,980 tokens; answer entropy 0.23 to 2.79. MATH-500: accuracy 83.2% standard vs 78.3% at 16,109 tokens. Parallel thinking at 16K budget about 22% above Wait-and-think-more (text elsewhere says up to 20%).
limits: Mid-size distilled models only (1.5B, 7B, 8B); no 32B or 70B.
agent_relevance: Argues for capped sequential thinking plus a few restarts. But G4 says one-model samples are not independent, so voting is a hint only.

source: Marjanovic et al. (2025) DeepSeek-R1 Thoughtology: Let's think about LLM Reasoning
finding: R1 chains have a fixed anatomy: problem definition, a long bloom cycle (decompose, first answer), reconstruction cycles (re-bloom = new approach; rumination = short repeats of old ones), then final decision. Each problem has a sweet-spot length; beyond it accuracy falls. Rumination is linked to inefficiency and sometimes lower accuracy.
numbers: 400 chains annotated (100 per task) with GPT-4o and a hand-checked prompt; rumination measured by 5-gram repetition rate and lexical entropy; GSM8K unconstrained about 1,388 tokens, budgets cut output nearly half with little loss. Correct answers were generally shorter than incorrect.
limits: Only the first 100,000 characters of a 400,000-character page read; one model family; stage labels produced by GPT-4o.
agent_relevance: Another episode code (bloom, re-bloom, rumination). Rumination (same approach re-examined) is a clean, code-checkable wild-goose-chase proxy: repeated n-grams or repeated approach.

source: Cuadron et al. (2025) The Danger of Overthinking: Examining the Reasoning-Action Dilemma in Agentic Tasks (AgentThink page)
finding: Overthinking in agent loops takes three forms: Analysis Paralysis, Rogue Actions, Premature Disengagement. A higher overthinking score goes with lower resolve rate; reasoning models overthink more than non-reasoning ones. Picking the lower-overthinking trajectory helps.
numbers: 4,018 trajectories on SWE-Bench Verified; choosing the solution with lower overthinking score improves performance by 'almost 30%' and cuts compute cost 43%.
limits: Project page only; scale of the score, correlation size, model list and the exact comparison base (relative vs absolute 30%) not stated.
agent_relevance: The agent-level counterpart of episode analysis; failure classes map to our states (stuck planning, acting without grounding, quitting early). Overthinking score could be an extra impasse input.

source: TRACE authors (2025): Do LLMs Really Need 10+ Thoughts for 'Find the Time 1000 Days Later'? Towards Structural Understanding of LLM Overthinking
finding: Splits chains into sub-thoughts, labels relations with gemini-2.5-pro, and clusters progress graphs into two overthinking patterns, Explorer and Late Landing (right answer found early, long wandering after). Defines overthinking by utility, not length. A simple self-looping stop heuristic recovers much of the saving.
numbers: 14 models, 6 domains; thinking uses 5 to 20 times more compute on simple tasks. Qwen3-235B GSM8k: 74.75% non-thinking vs 91.50% thinking, 118.1 vs 1,021.7 words; about 80% of the extra compute gives no gain. Temporal-L3: K=2 loop-stop gives 62.23% (length 2,722 to 1,315 words) for 235B and 68.90% (4,000 to 1,874) for 32B; Qwen3-32B K=3 reaches 80.18%, about 33 points below thinking mode, cost down about 40%. Convergence after the 8th sub-thought.
quote: models waste 5-20x more compute on simple tasks without accuracy gains
limits: Only the first 100,000 of 135,100 characters read; four large open models for patterns; greedy single runs; one task for the management study; LLM rater; clustering threshold 0.3 unvalidated.
agent_relevance: Late Landing is the pattern our detector should catch: answer already found, then Explore/Verify churn. Rule: stop after K repeated intermediate answers.

source: Bogdan, Macar, Nanda, Conmy (2025) Thought Anchors: Which LLM Reasoning Steps Matter?
finding: Sentences labelled by function show that planning and uncertainty-management (backtracking) sentences have the largest causal effect on the final answer by resampling, not computation sentences. Forced-answer importance ranks computation highest instead, so the method of measuring matters.
numbers: R1-Distill-Qwen-14B; 20 MATH problems solved 25 to 75% of the time; 40 traces of about 144 sentences; 100 rollouts per sentence. Label shares: active computation 32.7%, fact retrieval 20.1%, plan generation 15.5%, uncertainty management 14.0%, problem setup 2.4%, final answer 0.7%. Split-half reliability of receiver-head scores r = 0.84.
limits: Preliminary; 95% CI on accuracy up to about +/-10% with 100 rollouts; position confounds; single case study; only first 100,000 of 124,000 characters read.
agent_relevance: Suggests where to intervene: at plan and uncertainty sentences, the high-leverage episode boundaries, not in computation.

source: Gandhi et al. (2025) Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners
finding: Four human-like behaviors (verification, backtracking, subgoal setting, backward chaining) decide whether a base model can improve under RL. Priming Llama with examples containing these behaviors lets it match Qwen. The behaviors matter more than correct answers in the priming data.
numbers: Countdown game, Qwen-2.5-3B vs Llama-3.2-3B; priming with incorrect but well-structured solutions performs about as well as correct ones (abstract gives no numbers).
limits: Abstract page only; one game plus some pretraining data; training-based, not scaffold-based.
agent_relevance: Same behaviors as our operators (verify, backtrack, subgoal, work backward). Supports putting them in the scaffold for models that lack them, e.g. small models.

source: Venhoff et al. (2025) Understanding Reasoning in Thinking Language Models via Steering Vectors
finding: Behaviors such as backtracking, uncertainty estimation, example testing and adding knowledge each have a steering direction; turning them up or down changes how often they appear in a chain.
numbers: Steering on DeepSeek-R1-Distill Qwen-14B, Qwen-1.5B, Llama-8B; layers e.g. 29 for Qwen-14B, 12 for Llama-8B; evaluated on 50 unseen tasks, greedy decoding, 1,000-token limit. No accuracy change reported.
limits: Measures behavior frequency, not correctness; only R1-distill family; labels from GPT-4o with some errors.
agent_relevance: Not usable with API models. Confirms the behaviors are separable units, which supports episode-level control from outside by prompt.

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: Simple test-time scaling
finding: Budget forcing: end thinking early, or append 'Wait' to make the model continue and re-check. This is a code-side episode control at the end of a chain.
numbers: s1-32B fine-tuned on 1,000 examples; with budget forcing AIME24 goes from 50% to 57%; beats o1-preview by up to 27% on MATH and AIME24.
limits: Abstract page only; later work (c16) shows gains reverse at long lengths.
agent_relevance: Simple precedent for program-triggered continuation. Pair with a cap to avoid the decline shown in c16.

source: Li et al. (2025) vs ThinkARM (2025) relation: what was and was not tested
finding: ThinkARM's related-work section says its taxonomy and its use differ from Li 2025: sentence level only, Answer added, 15 models, correctness and efficiency case studies, automatic annotation at scale. No independent group had replicated the episode-to-correctness result in the sources I could open.
numbers: Li 2025: 38 traces from 1 model; ThinkARM: 1,500 traces from 15 models.
limits: Same lab (Zhou group, Maryland) for both; correctness result is from a 500-trace case study only. A search for third-party follow-ups returned nothing opened.
agent_relevance: The central claim (Explore not stabilised means failure) is single-lab evidence [S]. Test on our own logs before using it as a guardrail.

source: Capable yet Parsimonious: Extracting and Characterizing Hidden Chain-of-Thought in Frontier Models (2026)
finding: Reportedly uses an LLM judge to put each reasoning unit into one episode class and compares models by step type and reasoning tree. Search snippet says the original episode prompt lacked guidance for boundaries Plan vs Explore and Verify vs Monitor. Claims one frontier model reaches a correct trajectory earlier.
numbers: No quantitative results on the abstract page (33 pages, 14 figures).
limits: Abstract only; extracted reasoning may be post-hoc rationalisation (authors' own caveat); single v1 preprint; model name could not be verified.
agent_relevance: Third-party use of the episode code on newer models, but treat as unverified. The Plan vs Explore and Verify vs Monitor ambiguity matches our own labelling risk.

source: Pi Loop Police and Pi Antiloop (open-source agent loop guards, 2026)
finding: Search snippets only: two-layer detector, character repeats plus a paragraph-opening fingerprint, catches a loop on the third repetition; the other tool escalates warning, force break, abort. Code fences are skipped to avoid false alarms.
numbers: No measured detection accuracy or false-positive rate published.
limits: Not opened; vendor README, no evaluation.
agent_relevance: Practical template for a coded wild-goose-chase detector: repeat count, similarity, no-progress runs, escalating response. Needs our own false-positive test.

source: Schoenfeld (1985) Mathematical Problem Solving, human control findings as cited by Li et al. 2025
finding: The Li 2025 background section (opened) says Schoenfeld's episode coding of student protocols found weak solvers start exploring without adequate analysis or planning, which led them down unproductive paths; success depended on control at episode boundaries. I could not open the 1985 book or confirm the often-quoted 60% wild-goose-chase figure.
numbers: None confirmed this session.
limits: Second-hand through Li et al.; web search for the 60% figure returned nothing relevant.
agent_relevance: Origin of the impasse detector idea: unmonitored Explore with no Analyze or Plan before it is the human failure signature. Check the 1985 text before quoting a number.

source: Survey: Towards a Mechanistic Understanding of Large Reasoning Models (2026) and post-answer waste figures
finding: Search summary only: accuracy rises then falls with reasoning length; models give long chains to easy problems and short ones to hard problems; one cited paper measures 41 to 52% of reasoning tokens spent after the model already committed to its final answer.
numbers: 41 to 52% of reasoning tokens after answer commitment (second-hand).
limits: Not opened; the 41 to 52% figure source not identified.
agent_relevance: If confirmed, supports a 'stop at the first stable answer' rule; verify source first.
